subjects.displayTitle: The soul as a mirror: inner treasure and reflected light
subjects.introduction: Why, Bahá’u’lláh asks on God’s behalf, does a soul made noble abase itself? Behind the question stand a lamp with light already placed inside, a treasure latent in every being, a human reality on which all the divine names have been focused as on a mirror. Yet the image is as humbling as it is exalting. A mirror makes no light of its own; it needs the sun, a surface free of dust and rust, and a steady turning toward its source. Malice and vain imaginings settle on it like grime, and no mirror can clean itself. Nor is reflection a private glow. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá expects the rays to show in speech, conduct and deeds, in justice and generosity, and in hearts that meet and pass the light along. The same figure explains how the soul lights the body and survives it. Paul’s picture of beholding divine glory and being changed into its likeness invites comparison with this discipline of attention. The path leads on to knowledge of self, to the image of God in the human reality, and to purity of heart.
subjects.arc: Begin with human nobility and its practical expression; explore the mirror’s light, limits, and cultivation; follow the relationship of hearts and the soul’s connection with the body; then return through comparative voices to prayer and service.

order.why: Open with the Hidden Words’ affirmation of love, light, nobility, and joy within.
shortened: Thou art My lamp and My light is in thee. Get thou from it thy radiance and seek none other than Me. For I have created thee rich and have bountifully shed My favor upon thee.

Noble I made thee, wherewith dost thou abase thyself? Out of the essence of knowledge I gave thee being, why seekest thou enlightenment from anyone beside Me? Out of the clay of love I molded thee, how dost thou busy thyself with another? Turn thy sight unto thyself, that thou mayest find Me standing within thee, mighty, powerful and self-subsisting.

order.why: Invite attention to the treasures latent in one’s being.
Make reflection concrete in speech, behavior, and deeds.
Read spiritual nature through justice, generosity, kindness, and charitable action.
shortened: This spiritual nature, which has come to exist through the grace of the divine Reality, is the sum of all perfections and proceeds from the breath of the Holy Spirit.  It is the divine perfections; it is light, spirituality, guidance, exaltation, high-mindedness, justice, love, generosity, kindness to all, and charitable deeds:  it is life upon life.  This spiritual nature is an effulgence of the splendours of the Sun of Truth.

order.why: Explore latent capacities and the assistance that awakens them.
shortened: Upon the reality of man, however, He hath focused the radiance of all of His names and attributes, and made it a mirror of His own Self.

These energies with which the Daystar of Divine bounty and Source of heavenly guidance hath endowed the reality of man lie, however, latent within him, even as the flame is hidden within the candle and the rays of light are potentially present in the lamp. The radiance of these energies may be obscured by worldly desires even as the light of the sun can be concealed beneath the dust and dross which cover the mirror. Neither the candle nor the lamp can be lighted through their own unaided efforts, nor can it ever be possible for the mirror to free itself from its dross. It is clear and evident that until a fire is kindled the lamp will never be ignited, and unless the dross is blotted out from the face of the mirror it can never represent the image of the sun nor reflect its light and glory.

order.why: Distinguish reflected light from the sun entering a mirror.
shortened: And thou shalt find My meaning within thyself: When the mirror is polished and is turned towards the sun, it can see the sun, that is, the effulgence of its rays, within itself. This doth not mean that the sun hath entered the mirror, for the sun remaineth at the zenith of its sanctity; it neither descendeth nor ascendeth.

order.why: Turn the image outward toward recognizing revelation in another person.
Consider love reflected from heart to heart.
Read the purification of malice and the signs within humanity.
shortened: Wert thou to cleanse the mirror of thy heart from the dust of malice, thou wouldst apprehend the meaning of the symbolic terms revealed by the all-embracing Word of God made manifest in every Dispensation, and wouldst discover the mysteries of divine knowledge.

Even as He hath revealed: "We will surely show them Our signs in the world and within themselves." Again He saith: "And also in your own selves: will ye not then behold the signs of God?" And yet again He revealeth: "And be ye not like those who forget God, and whom He hath therefore caused to forget their own selves." In this connection, He Who is the eternal King -- may the souls of all that dwell within the mystic Tabernacle be a sacrifice unto Him -- hath spoken: "He hath known God who hath known himself."

order.why: Keep divine incomprehensibility beside the sign deposited in created things.
shortened: How utterly independent hath His sacred Essence been from the comprehension of all created things, and how immeasurably exalted shall it remain above the praise of all dwellers of earth and heaven! Through the pure bounty of His grace and the sublime excellence of His mercy, He hath deposited within all things that are seen and known the sign of His knowledge, that no thing might be deprived of recognizing His presence according to its capacity and station.

order.why: Explore the mirror, veiled candle, and heart as a dwelling of mysteries.
shortened: A pure heart is as a mirror; cleanse it with the burnish of love and severance from all save God, that the true sun may shine therein and the eternal morning dawn.

73 O friend, the heart is the dwelling-place of eternal mysteries: Make it not the home of fleeting fancies. Waste not the treasure of thy precious life occupied with this swiftly passing world. Thou comest from the world of holiness: Bind not thine heart to the earth. Thou art a dweller in the court of reunion: Choose not the homeland of the dust.

order.why: Read revelation as awakening awareness of a trust and unlocking hearts.
Consider the twofold capacity for recognition and reflection.
Read the human reality as a seat of signs of divine perfections.
shortened: Now, the world of existence, indeed every created thing, proclaims but one of the names of God, but the reality of man is an all-encompassing and universal reality which is the seat of the revelation of all the divine perfections. That is, a sign of each one of the names, attributes and perfections that we ascribe to God exists in man.

Thus man is a perfect mirror facing the Sun of Truth and is the seat of its reflection. The splendour of all the divine perfections is manifest in the reality of man, and it is for this reason that he is the vicegerent and apostle of God.

order.why: Explore distinct emphases of divine names and the limits of human knowing.
shortened: It is the mirror with the disposition to reflect all of the conflicting and opposing Names and is the source of the revelation of all of the Attributes of Divinity and Lordship.
However although he is the dawning-place of the manifestation of all the Names and Attributes, one of the Divine Names is manifested most strongly and appears most intensely [in each person].

For however much detached minds and pure souls seek to penetrate the worlds of Inner Knowledge, their understanding will never penetrate more than that station which is a sign pointing towards the Monarch of Primal Oneness which He has placed as a trust within the reality of man.  And however much they may fly with triumphant wings in the limitless space of what is knowable and observable, they will read naught but the letters of the book of their own selves.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s account of self-knowledge and signs in its own theological language.
shortened: And the Messenger of God said: "He among you who best knows himself best knows his Lord."

All souls are as mirrors, and He is manifest to the mirrors through the mirrors. He is the One, the sign of God and His description. And for all things this soul exists - whoso knoweth it hath known his Lord.

The meaning is that there is no way unto God except through recognition of this soul, which is the same as the recognition of the Lord, for a thing cannot be comprehended beyond its source. Whoso knoweth his own self through the attributes of his Creator knoweth Him, and that description is the description of the Lord - there is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Most Exalted, the Most Great.

order.why: Consider nearness through character while preserving the transcendence of the Essence.
Read divine nearness and human unawareness together.
Connect creation through love with the command to fellowship.
Read the purpose of suffering as concord and the fruit of primal oneness.
Consider generosity as a name whose traces appear in human beings.
Read wisdom, craft, and insight as differing reflections of the Word.
shortened: Its appearance in every mirror is conditioned by the colour of that mirror. For instance, when its light is cast upon the mirrors of the hearts of the wise, it bringeth forth wisdom. In like manner, when it manifesteth itself in the mirrors of the hearts of craftsmen, it unfoldeth new and unique arts, and when reflected in the hearts of those that apprehend the truth, it revealeth wondrous tokens of true knowledge and discloseth the verities of God’s utterance.

order.why: Keep the reported examples of knowledge, life, sight, and will as signs.
Read the reported account of divine qualities in individuality.
shortened: All these attributes are the characteristics of the unchangeable individuality and are divine in origin. These qualifications are loved by all, for they are emanations of the father. They are the significance of his name and attributes, the direct ray of which illuminate the very essence of these qualifications.

order.why: Consider spiritual education as development of the divine image.
shortened: He must also impart spiritual education, so that minds may apprehend the metaphysical world, breathe the sanctified breaths of the Holy Spirit, and enter into relationship with the Concourse on high, and that human realities may become the manifestations of divine blessings, that perchance all the names and attributes of God may be reflected in the mirror of the human reality, and the meaning of the blessed verse, "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness" may be realized.

order.why: Read the reported purpose of teachers and books as training human realities.
shortened: The more the world of humanity develops, the more the effulgences or emanations of Divinity will become revealed, just as the stone, when it becomes polished and pure as a mirror, will reflect in fuller degree the glory and splendor of the sun.

The mission of the Prophets, the revelation of the Holy Books, the manifestation of the heavenly Teachers and the purpose of divine philosophy all center in the training of the human realities so that they may become clear and pure as mirrors and reflect the light and love of the Sun of Reality.

order.why: Consider being illumined so as to guide others.
shortened: God sent His Prophets into the world to teach and enlighten man, to explain to him the mystery of the Power of the Holy Spirit, to enable him to reflect the light, and so in his turn, to be the source of guidance to others.

order.why: Read the relation of letters to the Word through the example of the Apostles.
Distinguish primary mirrors of revelation from those reflecting their glory.
shortened: Every one of them is a mirror of God, reflecting naught else but His Self, His Beauty, His Might and Glory, if ye will understand. All else besides them are to be regarded as mirrors capable of reflecting the glory of these Manifestations Who are themselves the Primary Mirrors of the Divine Being, if ye be not devoid of understanding.

order.why: Consider derived light through the moon and sun image.
shortened: Today all pure realities and abstract essences are like moons that must derive their light from the Sun of God's Cause and the gleaming Star of God's Law.

order.why: Read dependence on the sun and the problem of one’s own coloring.
Place attention on the light rather than the mirror that receives it.
shortened: Souls are like unto mirrors, and the bounty of God is like unto the sun. When the mirrors pass beyond all coloring and attain purity and polish, and are confronted with the sun, they will reflect in full perfection its light and glory. In this condition one should not consider the mirror, but the power of the light of the sun, which hath penetrated the mirror, making it a reflector of the heavenly glory.

order.why: Read the reported reminder that a mirror’s brightness is received.
shortened: We may look at a mirror and praise it, and say how wonderfully bright it is, and what a beautiful light is in it, but the mirror of itself is dark. It is only bright because it reflects the light; if it is dusty or not clear, it will not reflect much light.
The light of God is also reflected from a stone, and from the whole face of nature.

order.why: Keep the reported account of worldly perfections as reflections.
shortened: The rays of the sun shine forth from the mirror when it is exposed to the sun, although the mirror of itself is dark. The light which we see in the mirror is but the effect of the power and grace of the sun. In the same way, the visible world is altogether imperfect; all the virtues and all the perfections which appear in this world are the reflections of the perfections of God.

order.why: Read the call for all mirrors to face the sun.
Consider differing reflections and the heart reserved as a dwelling.
Read the selection of hearts as seats of revelation.
shortened: He hath chosen out of the whole world the hearts of His servants, and made them each a seat for the revelation of His glory. Wherefore, sanctify them from every defilement, that the things for which they were created may be engraven upon them.

order.why: Keep hearts as the stated object of the mission.
Consider utterance as a key to opening the city of the heart.
shortened: The things He hath reserved for Himself are the cities of men's hearts, that He may cleanse them from all earthly defilements, and enable them to draw nigh unto the hallowed Spot which the hands of the infidel can never profane. Open, O people, the city of the human heart with the key of your utterance.

order.why: Read the heart as earth containing seeds of knowledge and love.
Consider the heart as dawn and treasury.
shortened: O Gawhar! The Ancient Beauty gazeth upon thee from the Most Great Scene and saith: The heart hath been the dawning-place of the lights of My countenance and the treasury of the pearls of My love.

order.why: Preserve the brief image of the Book manifest in the human temple.
Read the reported sanctuary and throne images for soul and reason.
Consider spiritual realities as concealed light.
Read niche, glass, and flame as a connected image of illumination.
shortened: O thou who hast obtained guidance from the light of the truth! The human temple is like unto a niche, and the heart is like unto a glass globe, and the love of God is like unto the light within that glass. When that lamp is ignited, the globe becometh illumined and the physical niche also becomes full of light and brilliance.

order.why: Distinguish the rational soul’s powers from the illumination of faith.
shortened: But the human spirit, unless it be assisted by the spirit of faith, cannot become acquainted with the divine mysteries and the heavenly realities. It is like a mirror which, although clear, bright, and polished, is still in need of light. Not until a sunbeam falls upon it can it discover the divine mysteries.

order.why: Read the reported question about placeless spirit and reception of light.
Keep the reported answer identifying the mirror with body and brain as a distinct account.
shortened: Question: What is meant by the Mirror for Divine Reflection?
Abdu'l Baha: "Mirror" is the whole body, the brain in particular.

order.why: Read the interpretation of inward presence through education and reflection.
shortened: Thou hast asked about the statement in the Hidden Words, which reads:  "O Son of Spirit!  Turn thy face so that thou mayest find Me within thee, Powerful, Mighty and Supreme."

This is evident that, when the hearts are purified and through divine education and heavenly teachings become the manifestors of infinite perfections, they are like clear mirrors, and the Sun of Truth will reflect with might, power and omnipotence in such a mirror, and to such an extent that whatever is brought before it is illumined and ignited.

order.why: Keep the reported explanation of standing within as reflection in a clear mirror.
Read the question and answer about Pentecost as metaphor and analogy.
shortened: Question: It is recorded in the Gospels that the Holy Spirit descended upon the Apostles. What was the manner and meaning of this descent?

Answer: The descent of the Holy Spirit is not like the entrance of air into the human body. It is a metaphor and an analogy rather than a literal image or account. That which is intended is like the descent of the sun into a mirror, that is, when its splendour is reflected therein.

order.why: Explore why relationships of intelligible realities are not bodily entry.
shortened: The descent of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles means that that glorious and divine grace cast its light and splendour upon their realities.

Thus, as it is evident and established that intelligible realities do not enter or inhere, it follows that it is in no wise possible for the Holy Spirit to ascend, descend, enter, exit, commingle or inhere. At most it appears as the sun appears in a mirror.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s prayerful account of being a mirror.
Read the Bab’s rhetorical question about clay and the divine sign.
Preserve the source’s distinction between inaccessible Mystery and its representative.
shortened: In truth, the praise of these servants has not been and is not worthy of the Concealed Mystery, the Hidden Secret, and the Protected Symbol. The path to the impenetrable Mystery is blocked and the quest rejected. However, praise, gratitude, mention and glorification are befitting of Him Who stands in the place of Truth, glorified be His Glory. He is the Dawning-Place of supreme attributes and the Dayspring of the Most Beautiful Names. This most exalted station and loftiest summit and ultimate goal ended with the Seal of the Prophets, may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him.

order.why: Keep the reported philosophical account of Logos and emanation attributed.
shortened: The creation is an emanation of light of the eternal Light. The description of the Logos (Soul of the world) as effulgence of light also goes back to ar-Razi. From the throne of the Glory of the Creator His Light shines on the Soul emanated from Him (Soul of the world, Logos) and is then further reflected on the individual soul, so that it too would reflect it and look back in longing to its divine origin in Him!"

order.why: Read the reported account of development, individuality, and reflection.
shortened: When in the course of evolution the stage of thought and reason has been reached, the human mind acts as a mirror reflecting the glory of God.

The face of nature is illumined, the grass, the stones, the hills, and valleys shine; but they shine not of themselves, but because they reflect the rays of the sun. It is the sun which shines. In the same way, our minds reflect God.

order.why: Consider the reported microcosm and macrocosm analogy in its philosophical setting.
Keep the reported comparison of humanity and nature as the address’s argument.
Read the source’s polemical challenge concerning the divine trust without generalizing its accusation.
Consider the reported account of study bringing hidden capacities to light.
Read daily growth in receptivity and clarity.
Consider polishing as the stated duty of the heart.
shortened: The most important thing is to polish the mirrors of hearts in order that they may become illumined and receptive of the divine light.

Therefore, our duty lies in seeking to polish the mirrors of our hearts in order that we shall become reflectors of that light and recipients of the divine bounties which may be fully revealed through them.

order.why: Read the reported practice of supplication as a form of polishing.
shortened: The heart of man is like a mirror that is covered with dust, and to cleanse it one must continually pray to GOD that it may become clean, and the act of supplication is the polish which erases all worldly desires. The delight of supplicating and entreating before GOD cuts one's heart from the world. When the taste of man is nourished by honey, he never likes to taste any other sweetmeat.

order.why: Connect concentrated prayer to the transformation of daily life.
shortened: The worshipper must pray with a detached spirit, unconditional surrender of the will, concentrated attention and a magnetic spiritual passion. His innermost being must be stirred with the ethereal breezes of sanctification. If the mirror of his soul is polished from the dross of all desires the heavenly pictures and sidereal images of the Kingdom of God will become fully reflected therein. Then he will be given the power, to translate these celestial forms into his own daily life and the lives of many thousands.

order.why: Read pure intention and freedom from self-love in a collective setting.
shortened: O people of Persia! The heart is a divine trust; cleanse it from the stain of self-love, adorn it with the coronal of pure intent, until the sacred honor, the abiding greatness of this illustrious nation may shine out like the true morning in an auspicious heaven.

order.why: Keep the reported identification of rancor and attachment as dust.
shortened: Like unto a mirror, man's heart and mind must be purified, clarified and polished. Any dust or rust that may be on it such as attachment to this nether world, the turning of man's face away from God, sin or lust, animosity and rancor-all these must be removed that the rays of the Sun of Truth may shine upon it in full splendor and may be reflected there-from with full effulgence.

order.why: Read the command to remove vain imaginings.
shortened: Ye are the mirrors of My attributes - polish your hearts from the rust of vain imaginings.

order.why: Consider knowledge as the means of continual burnishing.
shortened: The hearts of the servants are mirrors of God - they must at all times be cleansed and sanctified with the burnishing of His knowledge.

order.why: Read refinement from heedlessness and harmful qualities.
Keep the concise relation between polishing and radiance.
shortened: Now, the more you polish the mirror, the more will the light of the Sun of Truth shine upon it and the greater will be its radiance.

order.why: Preserve the companion statement with its own identity.
shortened: The more a mirror is polished, the more will the rays of the sun be reflected therein.

order.why: Read the reported priority of removing rust.
shortened: First we must make ourselves receptive, then the bounties of God descend upon us. The mirror must become clear from rust first then the sun with all its glory will be reflected therein.

order.why: Consider the reflected image upon a transparent heart.
Read the appearance of signs in purified mirrors.
Join purification with turning toward the light.
Read the reported need to keep the heart directed toward God.
shortened: One should constantly turn the mirror of his heart squarely toward God so that the Light of the Sun of Truth may be reflected there.

order.why: Consider how the object faced shapes what a mirror reflects.
Read attunement to revelation as participation and benefit.
shortened: Even as a mirror, the reality of man should be attuned to, partake of and benefit from the Revelation of God.

order.why: Join finding receptive hearts with cultivating one’s own.
shortened: Therefore, that kind friend must find pure hearts that, like mirrors, may capture the true image of man. O seeker of truth! Polish the mirror of your heart clean of the rust and dust of this mortal world and turn it toward the celestial realm on high, that through the attractive power of the love of God, the exalted images of the Abha Kingdom and the effulgent lights of the Supreme Being may become reflected therein.

order.why: Read the reported hope for hearts directed heavenward.
Keep the brief reported summons to reflect one sun.
shortened: Your hearts must be like mirrors brightly polished, which reflect the light of the One sun.

order.why: Read the reported contrast of stone and clear mirror as a spiritual analogy.
Consider the warning against leaving the inner reality unillumined.
shortened: My point is this: the inner reality of man must! mirror the light that shines upon it from the rays of the Sun of Truth, otherwise it is no better than a black stone, darkness upon darkness.

order.why: Read the reported need for conscious receptivity and spiritual susceptibilities.
shortened: The spirit of man must acquire its bounties from the Kingdom of God in order that it may become the mirror and manifestation of lights and the dawning point of divine traces, because the human reality is like the soil.

Similarly, the human spirit or reality of man, unless it becomes the recipient of the lights of the Kingdom, develops divine susceptibilities and consciously reflects the effulgence of God, will not be the manifestation of ideal bounties, for only the reality of man can become the mirror wherein the lights of God are revealed.

order.why: Keep the reported possibility of reflection across geographic distance.
Consider transformation as a gift deposited within the heart.
shortened: This transformation is made possible through the spiritual Power which is deposited in the heart [of] man by the hand of the Almighty. It is a Celestial Gift on the part of God to His own handiwork.

order.why: Read renewal through bounty and nurturing care.
Consider progress in perfections appearing within humanity.
Read the manifestation of attributes through all aspects of one’s being.
Consider the invitation toward a station of reflecting divine beauty.
shortened: He desireth for no one save that which will draw him nigh unto the sacred court, the station wherein whosoever entereth will behold himself as a mirror of His beauty, the Mighty, the Wondrous.

order.why: Read the call to become mirrors that learn the ways of the spirit.
Join self-remembrance, sharing, and a receptive heart.
shortened: O servant! Remember thyself, then remind the people of what God hath taught thee of His grace, then make thy heart a mirror wherein this hidden and radiant Beauty may be reflected.

order.why: Keep the reported aspiration to guide others and forget self-preoccupation.
shortened: "My most earnest hope is that in the service of God I may attain such a station in order to put those in the Way of God that they may attain the grace of self-sacrifice and wholly forget their own personality and their age. So long as the surface of a mirror is not clean from rust and dust, the radiance and effulgence of the sun can never be printed upon it.

order.why: Consider pure hearts attuned to one another.
shortened: When man's soul is rarified and cleansed, spiritual links are established, and from these bonds sensations felt by the heart are produced. The human heart resembleth a mirror. When this is purified human hearts are attuned and reflect one another, and thus spiritual emotions are generated.

order.why: Read confronting mirrors as an image of unity and affinity.
shortened: O thou who art uttering the mention of God! Know, that the pure hearts upon which the mysteries of the Kingdom of God are printed and pictured, are reflections one upon another and thus the one can discover the secrets of the other, because such hearts are only mirrors confronting each other on which the secrets of unity, affinity and concord are printed and reflected.

order.why: Preserve the companion account of love reflected between hearts.
shortened: When the lights of love shone forth from the Truth unto creation, His greatest signs were imprinted upon pure and luminous hearts, and the mirrors of hearts faced one another and reflected that manifest light.

order.why: Keep the reported claim of impressions communicated without language attributed.
Read the tradition of believer as mirror through the divine name.
shortened: O assured believer! Among the divine names in the Qur'an is "The Believer" (Al-Mu'min), as mentioned in the tradition "The believer is the mirror of the believer," meaning that the assured believer among the servants is the locus of manifestation of divine signs.

order.why: Consider unity binding hearts into a shared spiritual life.
shortened: He maketh the heart to dance for joy and filleth up the soul with an ecstasy of love and rapture. So intensely hath the glory of Divine Unity penetrated souls and hearts that all are now bound one to another with heavenly ties, and all are even as a single heart, a single soul. Wherefore reflections of the spirit and impressions of the Divine are now mirrored clear and sharp in the deep heart's core.

order.why: Read holy souls as distinct mirrors of one beauty.
Consider the reported hope for clearer perception beyond colored glass.
shortened: The light of truth has heretofore been seen dimly through variegated glasses, but now the splendors of Divinity shall be visible through the translucent mirrors of pure hearts and spirits.

order.why: Read the reported continuity of light through changing holders and gardens.
Consider love’s flame as guidance.
shortened: When the light of the love of God is burning in the mirror of the heart, that flame shows the way and guides to the Kingdom of the Word of God.

order.why: Read the reported distinction between passing pictures and the heart’s lasting image.
shortened: These things about here that you have pictured will all pass away, but the true picture is the one you take on the mirror of the heart.

order.why: Consider inward attention as recognition of love and nearness.
Keep the personal reassurance using dust and sweetness in its addressed setting.
shortened: You do not become sorrowful, you do not become grief-stricken, dust surely does not settle upon your noble mind, and gloom finds no path to your tender heart, for that heart is the dawning-place of love for the Abha Beauty, and that flower is infused with pure honey. What power has dust to affect that clear mirror, and what strength has bitterness to impart its taste to such intense sweetness?

order.why: Read the source’s account of detachment, illumination, and joy.
shortened: Therefore, when a person of pure heart and sanctified mind becomes, mirror-like, free from the rust of attachment to aught else but God, he derives light from the Sun of Reality, becomes a polished surface reflecting divine lights, becomes an unveiler of mysteries, becomes the joy of the righteous, attains to true existence, and is freed from all sorrow.

order.why: Consider the reported relation of spiritual inheritance and enduring life.
shortened: If he attains unto his heritage through divine wisdom, then he becomes a clear mirror in which the beauty of God is reflected; he has eternal life and becomes a participator of the sun of truth.

order.why: Read everlasting life through knowledge and recognition.
shortened: That life, however, which is mentioned in the Books of the Prophets and the Chosen Ones of God is the life of knowledge; that is to say, the servant's recognition of the sign of the splendours wherewith He Who is the Source of all splendour hath Himself invested him, and his certitude of attaining unto the presence of God through the Manifestations of His Cause. This is that blessed and everlasting life that perisheth not: whosoever is quickened thereby shall never die, but will endure as long as His Lord and Creator will endure.

order.why: Keep the reported account of the illumined spirit’s permanence.
Explore the soul’s influence and the body as its instrument.
shortened: Thus it becomes clear that the human reality's permanence and influence are not conditional on the physical frame. Rather, this physical frame is an instrument upon which the human spirit casts its rays, like the sun shining upon a mirror making it bright, and when the sun's connection to the mirror is cut off, the mirror becomes dark. Likewise, when the spirit's outpouring is cut off from the body, that instrument becomes idle.

order.why: Read the explicit distinction between bodily movement and the soul’s connection.
shortened: In regard to the phenomenon of death, know that the soul of man is sanctified and independent from material existence.

Therefore, the soul of man does not enter into this corporeal frame, but rather it has a connection to it. Death consists of the severing of that connection. That connection resembles the relationship between a mirror and the sun. The sun does not enter into or depart from the mirror, and does not incarnate itself therein, but has a connection to the mirror and is reflected within it. When that connection becomes severed, the mirror is deprived of its brilliance, loveliness, and charm.

order.why: Keep the concise sun-and-mirror analogy for spirit and body.
Uses the pure mirror to distinguish spiritual receptivity from physical proximity.
Consider placeless spirit without assigning it a bodily location.
shortened: For were you to search throughout the human body you would be unable to find a specific place or location for the spirit. The spirit is absolutely placeless and immaterial, but it has a connection with the body, even as the sun has a connection with this mirror: The sun occupies no place within the mirror but it has a connection with it.

order.why: Read the rational soul’s subsistence beyond a broken or dusty mirror.
shortened: Secondly, the rational soul, or the human spirit, does not subsist through this body by inherence---that is to say, it does not enter it, for inherence and entrance are characteristics of bodies, and the rational soul is sanctified above this. It never entered this body to begin with that it should require, upon leaving it, some other abode. No, the connection of the spirit with the body is even as the connection of this lamp with a mirror. If the mirror is polished and perfected the light of the lamp appears therein, and if the mirror is broken or covered with dust the light remains concealed.

order.why: Consider an intact source of light when its reflecting instrument breaks.
shortened: As to the human spirit, its likeness is that of a glass and the bounty of the sun. That is, the body of man, which is composed of the elements, is the most perfect form of composition and combination, the soundest arrangement, the noblest composition, and the most perfect of all existing things. It grows and develops through the animal spirit. This perfect body can be compared to a mirror and the human spirit to the sun: If the glass is shattered or the mirror destroyed, no harm befalls the outpouring grace of the sun, which continues unabated.

order.why: Keep the brief account of severing a connection.
Read the reported question and answer defining death through that connection.
Preserve the companion reported explanation of the temporary mirror.
shortened: When man dies, his relation with the body ceases. The sun is reflected in the mirror; the mirror reflects the light and brilliancy of the sun, but the sun does not reside in the mirror. It does not enter nor come out of the mirror, nevertheless one sees it in the mirror, so the soul reflects itself in the body.
The body is the temporary mirror; the spiritual soul suffers no change, no more than the sun does remaining eternally in its own station.

order.why: Read the argument against treating spirit as a fluid poured between vessels.
shortened: They conceive of the body as a vessel and the spirit as its contents, like water and cup, with the water being emptied from one cup and poured into another.  This is indeed a childish notion:  They do not reflect deeply enough to realize that the spirit is an entirely incorporeal thing, that it does not enter or exit, and that at most it is connected with the body as the sun is with the mirror.

order.why: Return to the source’s vision of earthly life illumined by guidance.
shortened: O ye the sincere loved ones of God! The light of Divine Guidance hath shone forth from the dawning-place of Divine Unity and enlightened the whole earth with the radiance of its vernal glory. It hath made the earth to be the envy of Heaven and the world of being to be the desire of the realms of the Placeless.

order.why: Read gratitude through both mirror and fertile-soil images.
shortened: Therefore, give thanks unto God that thy pure heart was a polished mirror that became illumined with the lights of guidance, and thy soul was good and fertile soil that, through the outpourings of the clouds of grace, brought forth the flowers and sweet herbs of guidance.

order.why: Consider the prayer to embody virtues as reflected light.
shortened: We pray that all of us may become recipients of its bestowals, that we may be illumined by the lights of heaven, edified through the teachings of God and imbued with the virtues of divine character, as mirrors reflecting the light of the sun.

order.why: Keep the reported prayer for cleansed hearts.
shortened: May the mirrors of hearts be cleansed from dust in order that the Sun of Truth may be reflected therein.

order.why: Read the reported hope of reflecting Bahaullah’s beauty.
Consider the prayer for a pure and receptive heart.
Keep the brief petition for reflection of spiritual light.
shortened: And I beseech Him to make thy breast a clear mirror to reflect the light of the Spirit of God.

order.why: Read the prayer joining life, safety, evidence, and illumination.
shortened: O thou maid-servant of God! I supplicate and implore my Lord to strengthen thee by the Spirit of Life, make thee enter the Ark of Safety, and show thee the evident signs; that the veils of the people of suspicion may be rent asunder and the brilliant proof of God become manifest to all regions, and thy heart be made a clear mirror wherein are printed the Lights of the Kingdom of the earth and heaven.

order.why: Gather the capacities of heart, senses, speech, and action in prayer.
shortened: O Lord, make my spirit a cup overflowing with the wine of Thy love, and my heart a pure and shining mirror reflecting the sun of Thy Beauty, and my tongue speaking Thy remembrance, and my ear attentive to Thy call, and my eye perceiving Thy signs, and my nostrils perfumed by Thy fragrances, and my feet firm in Thy religion, and my heart steadfast in Thy Covenant, and my face illumined by the light of Thy knowledge.

order.why: Close the linked readings with a prayer that illumination might make the world a paradise.
Open the supplied readings with the clarification of self, soul, and reflected attributes.
shortened: All these terms are different ways of referring to the one great reality within man, that divine spark of Reality which is the secret of his superiority over the rest of creation. That Divine Spark of Reality is in the nature of a reflection of the Divine Attributes in man, just as the mirror reflects the light of the sun.

order.why: Keep the supplied distinction between human reflection and prophetic revelation.
Read the supplied rational-faculty fragment with its boundary status visible.
Keep the provisional translation on soul and spirit explicitly attributed.
Read the supplied description of inspiration as reflected grace.
shortened: This station is the greatest of all stations, for this connection of the spirit of man with God is like unto a mirror and the sun of reality is reflected in it.

This station is the station of heavenly inspiration and is called the station of the divine grace.  It signifies that the rays of the sun of reality are resplendent in the mirror and the attributes of the sun of reality are reflected therein.

order.why: Preserve the Bab’s supplied provisional passage and its unresolved ending.
Read the supplied sun-and-body image with its internal omission retained.
Keep the pilgrim-note analogy of a person and reflected image distinct.
Read the supplied Plotinus fragment as an outside philosophical voice.
Keep Izutsu’s account of comprehensive unity in its secondary interpretive setting.
shortened: Man, on the contrary, not only synthesizes all the forms of the Divine self-manifestation which are scattered over the world of Being, but also is conscious of this whole. This is why a true comprehensive unity is established by Man, corresponding to the Unity of the Absolute. Man is in this sense the Imago Dei. And because of this peculiarity, Man can be ... the 'vicegerent' of God on the earth.

order.why: Read the supplied Plotinus invitation toward inner beauty with its omission visible.
Keep al-Bistami’s ecstatic account in its quoted setting without equating its claims with other texts.
Preserve the supplied Upanishadic formulations and citations as a distinct tradition.
Read the supplied Gita passages concerning indwelling and divine qualities in their own terms.
Keep the supplied Quran text and citation as given, without silent correction.
Read the supplied Gospel passage concerning the Kingdom within.
Consider the supplied Christian mystical invitation to seek the Beloved near at hand.
Read the supplied hadith concerning the believing heart.
Preserve the split excerpt and citation exactly; do not silently transfer reference text into the quotation.
Return to the supplied statement concerning the heart as divine possession.
Consider hearts reached through revelation and utterance.
Close with people becoming keys that open the cities of hearts.

questions: How does the mirror image hold together human dignity, dependence, and the possibility of growth?
What distinctions do the readings make between reflected divine attributes and the divine Essence?
What might polishing and turning mean in the practice of prayer, study, speech, and relationships?
How does the mirror analogy change when it describes the soul and body rather than the heart and divine light?
How does Paul’s account of beholding and transformation illuminate the connection between attention and character?
Which connected subject on self-knowledge, the image of God, or purity of intention would help you explore how an inner capacity becomes useful to others?

references.label: 1 · 2 Corinthians 3:17–18 · Beholding and transformation
references.note: Read Paul’s connection of the Spirit with freedom, and of beholding divine glory with transformation into its image. Compare this with the compilation’s mirrors that need both clarity and light, and its call to embody what is received. What relationship between attention, grace, and changed character emerges from the comparison?

subjects.displayTitle: Health and healing: skill, compassion, and care for the whole person
subjects.introduction: To look after the sick, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, is one of the greatest duties. Bahá’u’lláh sends the ill to competent physicians and confirms material means with His own Pen; the physician He describes heals first through remembrance of God and then through medicine, marked by trustworthiness, tenderness and the fear of the Lord as much as by skill. Prayer and treatment are two ways of healing that do not quarrel, each fitted to a different kind of cause. Care also takes humbler forms: a quiet room, a single nurse, rest, good news at a bedside, the happiness ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls a great healer. The Samaritan who binds wounds, pays the innkeeper and promises to return shows mercy as sustained labour [1]. Health is never an end in itself but strength lent for service, which is why hearts can fall ill as bodies do and a whole world may be called an ailing patient. The way leads on through prayer for healing, through the moderation and balance a sound constitution rests on, and toward the Physician who comes for the sickness of humanity itself.
subjects.arc: Begin with compassionate and competent care; examine body and spirit, historical accounts and the purpose of health; widen healing into service and social renewal.

order.why: Ground the inquiry in the explicit use of competent physicians and material means.
Open with the shared duty of kindly attending the sick.
Name the moral qualities that make medical skill trustworthy.
shortened: For the physician, the first qualifications are: Good intentions, trustworthiness, tenderness, sympathy for the sick, truthfulness, integrity, and the fear of the Lord. With life and heart strive thou to be both a spiritual and physical physician.

order.why: Place preservation of life beside a concrete medical exception.
Introduce the relationship between physical treatment and prayer.
shortened: There are two ways of healing sickness, material means and spiritual means. The first is by the treatment of physicians; the second consisteth in prayers offered by the spiritual ones to God and in turning to Him. Both means should be used and practised.

Illnesses which occur by reason of physical causes should be treated by doctors with medical remedies; those which are due to spiritual causes disappear through spiritual means. Thus an illness caused by affliction, fear, nervous impressions, will be healed more effectively by spiritual rather than by physical treatment. Hence, both kinds of treatment should be followed; they are not contradictory.

order.why: Acknowledge how hard illness is to bear.
Set the labor of saving one life against the destruction of war.
Extend attention to poor people, strangers and those in need.
shortened: In treating the poor, the weak, the needy and the strangers, provide blessed healing and guide them to health and wellbeing. And in spiritual healing and guidance of human souls, breathe an effective breath - become a guide to every lost one, and free every prisoner of diseases of heart and soul from the darkness and bondage of the world of nature. Cast upon them rays of light and apply the greatest antidote, so that through destined grace you may provide immediate remedy to every deprived poisoned soul and become an easy cure for the incurable pain of error.

order.why: Show care taking practical form in rest, nourishment and access to treatment.
shortened: Due to lack of time to attend to the requirements of the patient regarding physician, medicine and nourishment, We have decided that he should return to 'Akka and rest there. We beseech God to adorn it with the ornament of healing and to change his illness into health. Verily, He hath power over whatsoever He willeth, and He is the Single, the One, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Make comfort and relief a concrete intention of service.
shortened: For instance, they must say, "Since the Blessed Beauty has willed that I be a servant of the world of humanity, then I will serve this patient, remedy his ills, sooth his pains, treat his injuries, and give him all the comfort he needs."

order.why: Attend to the patient’s need for quiet and limited visits.
Consider the value attributed to kindness and happiness.
shortened: Happiness is a great healer to those who are ill. In the East it is the custom to call upon the patient often and meet him individually. The people in the East show the utmost kindness and compassion to the sick and suffering. This has greater effect than the remedy itself.

order.why: Join professional care with comfort and gladness.
Develop the image of nursing with hope.
Affirm the dignity of medicine and its practitioners.
shortened: The science of medicine hath been, in the sight of God, the most distinguished and exalted of all sciences. Indeed, it is through His leave the preserver of human bodies from diverse ailments. Therefore, whosoever engageth in and acquireth this noble science is well-pleasing in the sight of God. Verily, the reward of him who healeth the servants is with God, the Lord of the worlds. And whatsoever he receiveth from the people is lawful and pure unto him.

order.why: Connect bodily health with the exercise of understanding.
Explore physical medicine as a model for spiritual service.
shortened: And since between physical medicine and spiritual wisdom there exists perfect correspondence and true similarity, exact in every detail, such that even the particular points between these two sciences are in complete agreement and harmony - there being absolutely no difference or disparity in the diagnosis of illnesses, the balancing of constitution, the arrangement of treatment, the care of the sick and ailing, and the kindness shown to the infirm and bedridden - therefore the spiritual physician who must arise to treat souls sick with inner maladies should take his cue from physical medicine in all treatments and proceed accordingly.

order.why: Restate the duty to seek skilled advice.
shortened: The decisive command of God is that the sick must consult a skilled physician and act upon whatever he prescribes.

order.why: Apply consultation even to a patient who is a physician.
Place treatment and trust in God together.
Show obedience to medical advice in a difficult separation.
shortened: O Afnan of the Sacred Tree! Your separation has affected us and day by day our longing increases. However, one must obey the command of God and submit to medical opinion. Thus, thou hast undertaken this journey to comply with His command and not for the sake of healing, since healing is in the hand of God, not in the hand of doctors.

order.why: Retain the reported appeal to competent counsel.
shortened: Whenever sickness prevails and health is disturbed, seek the counsel of a competent physician. Protection of one's well-being and health is repeatedly enjoined in the Qur'an.

order.why: Include the reported counsel concerning necessary surgery.
Examine the reported comparison with trained practical skills.
shortened: A.B.: The Blessed Beauty says that when man becomes ill he should refer to a doctor, for he knows how to diagnose the illness. However much a man may have done carpentering (or learned carpentering), the carpenter is always better. A learned man may try to become a chauffeur but he will not be like a real (trained?) chauffeur - one who has studied in college, naturally such a one is better.

order.why: Keep the historical call to learn modern medical techniques.
Recognize the work and sacrifice of medical study.
Include the individual vocational counsel favoring medicine and surgery.
Preserve the reported discussion of opportunities and scrutiny in practice.
Notice the reported example of discovery emerging from unsuccessful searches.
Present the text’s argument for animal research in its own terms.
shortened: As to vivisection, however, it is productive of scientific discoveries and medical advantages which contribute to the welfare of all mankind. Perhaps through the vivisection of one animal discoveries may be made which will become the cause of life to a billion people.

order.why: Retain the reported qualifications and concern with animal suffering.
Return to gentle handling of the patient.
shortened: You have permission to practice medicine, but on condition that you use gentle, mild remedies and that when administering them to the patient you turn to the Divine Threshold and with utmost sincerity of heart seek healing, and deal gently with the patient.

order.why: Place prayer at the threshold of clinical attention.
shortened: O thou loyal servant of God and thou spiritual healer of man! Whensoever thou dost attend a patient, turn thy face toward the Lord of the heavenly Kingdom, ask the Holy Spirit to come to thine aid, then heal thou the sickness.

order.why: Consider turning to prayer amid diagnostic uncertainty.
shortened: When difficulties and complexities arise in diagnosing diseases and afflictions, turn with complete attention to the Lord of Lords so that thou mayest become a remover of sorrows, and sometimes persevere in reciting the prayers of the Blessed Beauty which have been revealed from the Supreme Pen for the healing of diseases, that health may be attained.

order.why: Distinguish the remedies described for body and soul.
State the two dispensaries through a compact metaphor.
shortened: O possessor of the remedy for the afflicted!

Illnesses and diseases are of two kinds: physical and spiritual. For bodily ailments, the cure lies in the pharmacy of earthly physicians, while for spiritual maladies and afflictions, the remedy is found in the divine dispensary.

order.why: Read the recorded clinical examples with their historical terminology.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha: Diseases are of two kinds. There are some which are due to material cause, and such diseases should be treated according to material methods. For instance, supposing there shall be some sort of process in the liver that is tissue pathology. Its treatment should be entirely physical. On the other hand, another disease may be spiritual in character. For example, fear is a nervous disease resulting not from any material cause. It is psychological neurosis. That sort of disease has to be treated spiritually.

order.why: Keep the reported insistence that material injuries require material remedies.
shortened: Disease is of two kinds: (a) Material (b) Spiritual. For instance, a cut of the hand; if you pray for the cut to be healed, and do not stop it bleeding, you will not do much good, this needs a material remedy.

Sometimes if the nervous system is paralyzed through fear, a spiritual remedy is necessary. Madness, incurable otherwise, can be cured through prayer, but an abscess cannot be cured by prayer alone. Extreme cases need prayer.

order.why: Follow with the broken-bone example.
Clarify the reported use of remedies available in nature.
Retain the demonstration linking surgery and spiritual reliance.
Condense the reported cooperation of the two forms of healing.
shortened: There is spiritual healing and there is also material healing. Unless these two work together a cure is impossible. The material element is medicine; spiritual healing is of God.

order.why: Explore the question and answer on healing without medicine.
shortened: Know that there are four kinds of treatment and healing without medicine. Two are due to material causes and two to spiritual ones.

But the fourth kind is when healing is brought about through the power of the Holy Spirit. This depends neither upon physical contact, nor upon sight, nor even upon presence: it is not dependent upon any condition.

order.why: Introduce the affirmation of the Holy Spirit’s healing power.
Distinguish human prayer from divine bestowal.
shortened: We pray but God bestows healing. We do not make claims for ourselves.

order.why: Consider the reported variety of conditions through which healing is sought.
Keep the reported account of healing across distance.
shortened: The healing that is by the power of the Holy Spirit needs no special concentration or contact. It is through the wish or desire, and the prayer of the Holy Person. The one who is sick may be in the East, and the healer in the West, and they may not have been acquainted with each other - but as soon as that Holy Person turns his heart to God and begins to pray the sick one is healed.

order.why: Preserve the particular instruction on tenderness and prayer.
Read the direction for using the healing Tablet.
Move into a devotional affirmation of divine healing.
Introduce the Tablet of Medicine with its historical dietary counsels and physician’s vocation.
shortened: Say: O people! Eat not save when hungry, and drink not after retiring to sleep. Exercise in the open air strengthens the body's members, while eating to excess is a grave calamity. Abandon not treatment when it is needed, but cease it when health is restored.

O Physician! Heal the sick, first through the remembrance of thy Lord, the Lord of the Day of Mutual Calling, then through that which We have ordained for the health of the constitutions of the servants. By My life! The physician who hath drunk the wine of My love - his visit is healing, his breath is mercy and hope.

order.why: Read the explanation that refers food incompatibility to physicians.
shortened: What is meant is that if two incompatible foods are served together at the table, it is not permissible to partake of both. And this dependeth on one’s constitution and on whether the digestive system is weak or strong.
This is a matter that must be determined by physicians. Whatever foods physicians forbid a person to combine would be regarded as incompatible.

order.why: Examine the account of equilibrium and the future of medicine.
shortened: The science of medicine is still in its infancy and has not yet reached maturity. But when it reaches that stage, treatments will be administered with things that are not repulsive to the senses of taste and smell, that is, through foods, fruits, and plants that have an agreeable taste and a pleasant smell.

As to physical agents, which are the primary cause of illness, their effect is due to the following: The human body is composed of numerous elements according to a particular state of equilibrium. So long as this equilibrium is maintained, man is preserved from sickness, but should this fundamental balance, which is the central requirement of a sound constitution, be upset, the constitution will be disrupted and illnesses will supervene.

order.why: Retain the source’s discussion of moral and physical causes without assigning blame to patients.
Keep the reported dietary account beside the discussion of balance.
Retain the reported claim about natural diet as attributed speech.
Include the reported observation on fruit skins.
Preserve the dietary question and personal reply.
Keep the reported story’s economic and dietary reasoning identifiable as a story.
Explore restraint through the patient-and-medicine analogy.
Read the reported meaning of a bitter remedy.
Extend the analogy to love that is initially misunderstood.
shortened: A teacher traineth and reproacheth his pupils, and this proceedeth from love; yet the children are pleased at the teacher’s death. Thus, when they hear that the teacher hath fallen ill, they rejoice and make merry. Likewise, when the physician giveth the patient a bitter medicine, the patient crieth out and lamenteth, saying: "I wanted not this bitter draught," and counteth the physician as an enemy. The physician protecteth him, yet the patient complaineth and is not content. But this protective treatment springeth from love, while the patient’s complaint proceedeth from ignorance.

order.why: Distinguish created substances from appropriate use and medical necessity.
shortened: As to the meaning of that which is written in the Tablets: "I have chosen for thee whatsoever is in the heaven and the earth", this signifieth those things which are in accordance with the divine purpose and not the things which are harmful. For instance, one of the existing things is poison. Can we say that poison must be used as it hath been created by God? Nevertheless, intoxicating liquor, if prescribed by a physician for the patient and if its use is absolutely necessary, then it is permissible.

order.why: Read the cleanliness and abstinence passage with its historical comparative claims intact.
Connect outward cleanliness with spiritual refinement.
Retain one recorded account concerning abstinence and children.
Keep the separate parallel recollection without merging its identity.
Include the recorded critique of reliance on wine.
Emphasize learning how to protect children’s health.
shortened: Let them also study whatever will nurture the health of the body and its physical soundness, and how to guard their children from disease.

order.why: Retain the reported appeal to hygiene education.
Consider the source’s warning about transmission of disease.
Preserve the historical plague prescription as source material, not present treatment advice.
Include the reported approval of exercise.
Read the recorded concern about crowded urban living.
Preserve the individual account of a prescribed sea visit.
shortened: However, when I came to 'Akka, it was prescribed for me to go to the sea everyday and this was not possible in Yarkih.

order.why: Attend to the affectionate hope for recovery in another climate.
shortened: O thou my affectionate sister!

God be praised, according to what we hear the climate in that land hath proved not unfavourable. It is to be hoped that out of the grace of the Blessed Beauty thy illness will be completely cured and thou wilt return in the best of health, so that once again I may gaze upon that wondrous face of thine.

order.why: Examine the text’s account of uncertainty and individual differences in treatment.
shortened: For example, when one disease overtakes two people, one treatment suits this one and another medicine that one. In any case, the point is that no physician can yet definitively judge that this theriac will certainly benefit this patient.

Therefore, come and be a spiritual physician so that you may observe with certainty that the divine theriac and the greatest heavenly medicine are the cure for spiritual diseases and the means of deliverance from spiritual perils and ills, that you may be freed from doubt and uncertainty and enter the kingdom of certitude.

order.why: Keep the particular counsel about analysis and reliance in its source setting.
Retain the recorded discussion of medicine when treatment is unavailable.
Preserve the distinct reported description of circumstances without doctors.
Acknowledge change and illness as conditions of embodied life.
Include the candid report of fever.
Set physical exhaustion beside renewed inward strength.
Read the personal account of illness at sea and spiritual turning.
shortened: And now I am at sea, in utmost weakness and illness, but the healing of soul and heart, even body, is in turning to the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Preserve the testimony of rapid recovery as a personal account.
Keep the recollection of fever and recovery distinctly attributed.
Read the reported personal assurance in its particular encounter.
Retain the individual assurance of healing.
shortened: And as for thee, O precious handmaiden of God, be thou assured of healing from every ailment through the power of the Spirit from God.

order.why: Turn assurance into a prayer for aid.
shortened: I beseech God, glorified and exalted be He, to assist thee with a penetrating heavenly power that influences the realities of things, to grant thee that which thou lovest and with which thou art well-pleased, and to heal thee from every pain, ailment and disease.

order.why: Include the recorded relation between happiness and bodily condition.
shortened: Happiness has a direct influence in preserving our health while being upset causes illness.

order.why: Examine the reported contrast between bodily comfort and inward happiness.
Retain the reported warning about preoccupation with health.
shortened: If a man thinks too much of his health, he will become afflicted.

order.why: Hear the remembered childhood experience of musical treatment.
shortened: Once during my early childhood I became very sick. At the time, my family lived in Teheran. I was lying in bed in a semi-conscious state. After much consultation the Doctors agreed upon a course of "musical treatment." Before sunset they brought into my room an old man with a very long beard. He carried under his 'Aba' a guitar. He sat near my bed and immediately began to play and sing. All through the night he played and sang, now in high, resonant voice and again in sweet, soft strains. My soul was charmed with his music.

order.why: Keep the separate recorded claim concerning music.
Allow the account of comfort near death to broaden the meaning of relief.
Retain the personal interpretation of illness and solitude as attributed counsel.
Ask what the use of health contributes to human life.
Distinguish the two recorded intentions for caring for the body.
shortened: Looking after one's health is done with two intentions:
1st. Man may take good care of his body with the intention of satisfying his personal wishes.
2nd. Or he may look after his health with the good intention of serving humanity and of living long enough to discharge one's duty towards mankind.
The latter is most commendable.

order.why: Relate physical strength to service and mortality.
shortened: One must certainly seek physical health for spiritual health, that is, to serve the Cause of God. Otherwise what result has health? Eventually health will decline and one will pass from this world to the next.

order.why: Consider the reported importance of the effects of good health.
shortened: Of what benefit is physical well-being? If it is spent in service to the Cause of God and in mindfulness and awareness, then health has importance - otherwise, if this is not the case, what importance does it have? Those effects that result from good health, these are praiseworthy. Therefore health is acceptable and beloved, but in and of itself what importance does it have?

It is certain that it will decline. In the end, no matter how much you protect this body, no matter how much you nurture it, it will eventually deteriorate. No matter how much you repair this edifice, it will ultimately fall into ruin.

order.why: Distinguish temporary recovery from the text’s aspiration for lasting spiritual life.
shortened: O beloved physician! Physical healing is achieved through herbs, electuaries, essences and antidotes, and is temporary. Eventually the patient becomes weary of this abode of sorrows and must one day take flight to the eternal realm.

But spiritual healing and inner health and well-being are desired and beloved and the ultimate aspiration of those possessed of understanding hearts, for this is an eternal healing and everlasting life.

order.why: Read the strong contrast between temporary treatment and mortality.
shortened: How many sick ones you treated with herbs and essences, and how many patients confined to bed you granted health and comfort through the power of elements and spirits! But this health does not endure and this comfort is not lasting or established. It appears for a few days like a mirage but in reality does not exist. And if you truly observe, physical treatments are merely palliative rather than curative, and health is temporary not permanent, for ultimately this structure must necessarily collapse and in the end this health will certainly decline.

order.why: Affirm spiritual soundness in a person who remains physically ill.
shortened: Though thou art physically sick and ill, praise be to God thou art spiritually sound and healthy, nay rather, enjoying perfect health.
This body is a mine of diseases and the seat of diverse ailments. However much it may be safeguarded, ultimately the hosts of maladies will prevail and illnesses and pains will break down this frame.

order.why: Retain the reported emphasis on spiritual health amid bodily decline.
Keep the reported personal dietary example in its context.
Preserve the question about charity and the reply on impermanence.
shortened: She then asked, "Are these people who claim to surpass the other Christian sects in charity and good deeds to be considered possessors of a special excellence or are they one of the new sects of Christianity?"

"As to healing the ills of the body and caring for the sick and the poor. This is very good, but its effect or result is not a permanent one. For when a man is healed of one physical pain, another will sooner or later affect him; and finally as a result, bodily death will overtake him.

order.why: Read the recorded meaning of inquiries about spiritual health.
shortened: Therefore, whenever I inquire about your health I mean your spiritual health. That is fraught with importance. To the same degree that the material life has no importance, the spiritual life is of supreme moment. Then the heart is purified, the spirit gladdened with the Good-News of the Kingdom and the realm of morality will become the delectable paradise.

order.why: Extend that meaning into a prayer for humanity.
Retain the reported comparison between kinds of weakness.
Introduce the possibility of illness of the heart.
shortened: Deprive not thyself of the portion of striving, for hearts become ill just as bodies become ill.

order.why: Consider the difficulty of curing ignorance.
shortened: As the body will be cured from physical disease, in the same way the spirit will be cured of all spiritual diseases. A cure of physical disease is very easy, but the cure of spiritual disease is very difficult.
If one has fever and you give him medicine, the fever will vanish; but if the spirit is afflicted with the disease of ignorance it is difficult to remove that disease.

order.why: Distinguish recognizing a spiritual malady from treating it.
shortened: O physician, O beloved! When physical physicians diagnose an illness, the treatment becomes easy and the physician becomes very hopeful. But spiritual diseases, even when diagnosed, are difficult to treat.

order.why: Remember that a healer may also be ill.
shortened: Even now, while in a feverish state, this letter is being written to inquire after your condition, requesting that you write in detail. The physician heals others while he himself is sick. My condition should be inquired after, yet despite having a fever, I am thinking of the true friends.

order.why: Read the figure of incurable folly as a challenge to receptivity.
shortened: Every disease hath its remedy and every pain its cure, save the malady of foolishness which is an incurable affliction - "and though they should see every sign, they will not believe therein."

order.why: Introduce the two classes of physicians across sacred history.
shortened: O divine physician!

From the beginning of history until this day, there have existed two classes of physicians in the world - divine physicians and natural physicians - and in the books and scriptures it is recorded that there were blessed souls who were divine physicians and diagnosed spiritual ailments and treated them with divine theriac. Those physicians studied medicine in the divine school, therefore they diagnosed chronic diseases of human souls and even deadly illnesses of the world and prescribed treatments. Similarly, natural physicians came and underwent many hardships, nursed the sick, and treated physical ailments of the infirm.

order.why: Bring the two kinds of service together in a prayer.
Affirm care for bodies, spirits and wounded hearts.
Preserve the historical comparison used to encourage a physician’s further development.
Connect further medical study with a purpose of spiritual service.
shortened: This spiritual medicine is established and enduring, its influence everlasting and its gift heavenly.

And if you hasten to London to perfect physical medicine, let your purpose be to spread spiritual medicine in that northern clime, that perhaps you may guide a soul to the greatest guidance and grant healing from spiritual diseases.

order.why: Explore the common wisdom underlying two forms of healing.
shortened: For guidance is the medicine of the spirit and the cause of spiritual victories - it is healing for the soul and a remedy of joy and delight for the heart. When wisdom shines with spiritual radiance it becomes guidance, and when its lights beam upon the body it becomes medicine.

Therefore, one who combines these two qualities and possesses these two virtues - which in essence are one reality but appear as two realities in relation to the spiritual and physical worlds - is a perfect person.

order.why: Relate healing service to embodying divine counsels.
Consider the relation between attraction to God and vivifying others.
shortened: The treatment of bodies, drawing upon the outpourings of the All-Merciful and the confirmations of the Mighty, All-Knowing, will be realized for thee when thou art so attracted to God that thou givest spirit to spirits and life to hearts in this world of forms.

order.why: Encourage continued attention to hearts and bodies.
Picture service taking the form of nursing and visiting.
shortened: Especially if he is a sage and physician, his wisdom is greater, for he applies the supreme remedy and treats with the divine elixir. Sometimes he uses illness as a pretext to visit the sick, becomes their nurse, treats both body and soul, and applies an immediate cure. In short, this is true healing, this is wisdom, this is the gift.

order.why: Find the practitioner’s joy in another person’s progress.
shortened: The physician's joy and delight is in healing the sick, and the teacher's happiness and success is in the progress of the students in school. Each of the friends must be a knowing physician and a skilled healer.

order.why: Recognize balm applied to wounded hearts.
Read the prayer for growth as a spiritual healer.
Preserve the individual exhortation to concentrate on spiritual healing.
Connect inward health with responsibilities, family and service.
Consider Job and the image of a healing spring.
Widen the dispensary from an individual to the world.
shortened: O Nasru'l-Atibba! The true healing is the healing of hearts and the treatment of souls, for through it everlasting health is attained and the face becomes flushed with the heat of love for the Most Glorious Beauty. Through it heavenly life is made possible and immortality in the Most Glorious Kingdom is achieved.
Therefore, O physician, open wide the court of divine healing and establish a dispensary with the theriac of guidance. Take the pulse of creation and heal the ailing form of the world.

order.why: Introduce the divine elixir as an image for renewal.
Hear the urgency of becoming a spiritual physician.
shortened: Hasten to life before death, to spring before autumn, and to healing before sickness, that you may become a spiritual physician, healing all ills and diseases through the breath of the spirit in this praiseworthy century and this witnessed age.

order.why: Imagine lasting restoration through a life of service.
Include the call to become a source of healing to hearts.
Retain the text’s language of love and healing power.
shortened: Whosoever is filled with the love of Baha and forgets all things - the Holy Spirit breathes into his mouth and the spirit of life into his heart, the lights of verses shine from his face, words scatter like strings of pearls from his mouth, and he heals ills and sickness by the touch of his hand.

order.why: Keep the separate parallel wording and source identity.
Explore the envisioned relation between heavenly aspiration and material life.
Turn from individual illness to an ailing humanity.
shortened: Indeed, all humanity is endangered by diverse ailments and maladies, yet the remedy prescribed by the divine Skilled Physician is not heeded. Therefore, unskilled physicians are now holding sway, while they themselves are afflicted with incurable ailments.

order.why: Ask why a suffering world might reject its healers.
shortened: The body of the world is sick and the form of creation is ailing, while skilled physicians are considered worthless and despised by the patients. These patients flee from the physicians, and these sufferers are incurable.

order.why: Recognize the need for a skilled remedy for chronic social illness.
Read the chosen Physician as a bounty to humanity.
Introduce the image of a supreme remedy.
Identify the Covenant in this text’s diagnosis of collective illness.
Hear the urgent call for bandages and salves for the world.
shortened: O spiritual physician! The weak body of the world is afflicted with a hundred thousand chronic, fatal diseases, and the ailing existence of humanity is exposed to great dangers, restless and suffering.
Therefore, O physician, it is time for healing and treatment, it is time for bandages and salves, until divine confirmation determines what will transpire.

order.why: Attend to the treatment of hearts and souls.
shortened: O physician of the hearts of the loved ones of God!

Today severe illnesses and various ailments and maladies have overtaken the spiritual temples and hearts and souls of human beings. Therefore, with the help and favor of the Ancient Beauty, skilled physicians must treat them with the most great universal remedy.

order.why: Discusses the physician’s role in gladdening hearts as well as treating bodies.
Make kindness central in the image of the world as a hospital.
Read virtues and love as medicines freely dispensed.
shortened: Be a spiritual physician, become a heavenly doctor. Give the divine remedy to those sick in heart and soul, and guide the ailing ignorant ones to the divine hospital. Apply the tincture of the Abha Kingdom, use the antidote of the Supreme Concourse. Dispense freely the supreme theriac of divine virtues, and liberally bestow the greatest elixir of the love of God, so that you may give freshness and grace to the withered souls of the Turkmen, and with your Christ-like breath bring to life the spiritually dead among those tribes and peoples.

order.why: Retain the excerpt’s aspiration toward enduring healing.
shortened: O physician! Wisdom is the light of guidance, and the healing art is the antidote of the love of Baha. As much as thou canst, employ this divine medicine that thou mayest bestow eternal healing and effect an immediate cure.

A particle of this remedy is the cure for every ailment and the healing of every breast. It bestoweth such healing that illness shall never follow, and such a medicine that it becometh the remedy for every incurable disease.

order.why: Consider remedies fitted to differing patients.
Imagine service to the helpless through a growing community.
shortened: You are the unfailing remedy for the incurable pain of humanity and the swift cure for the disordered constitution of the horizons.

Ere long you shall become physicians to the helpless and educators in the school of seekers, for the Cause of God shall gain such strength that all will run after the physician like patients, and hasten like the wounded in search of the supreme healing balm.

order.why: Gather the social inquiry into a shared resolve to become a balm.
Let a prayer hold physical recovery and relief of sorrow together.
Pray for healing of seen and unseen affliction.
Close the source-linked readings with a plea for mercy.
Open the supplied selections with combining prayer and competent medical treatment.
Apply that counsel to a painful and apparently hopeless case.
Distinguish loving assistance from professional medical judgment.
Keep exceptional spiritual healing framed as a mysterious gift.
Close by inviting both physical help and spiritual care.

questions: How do the qualities asked of a physician change your understanding of what competent care involves?
What forms of practical assistance, quiet presence, or encouragement might best serve someone whose illness continues?
