How do the readings place prayer and medical treatment in relationship, and where do their differing contexts matter?
What changes when health is considered in relation to service, rather than only personal comfort or longevity?
How might the distinction between bodily illness and spiritual health help us avoid judging a person by their physical condition?
When the world is described as an ailing body, what responsibilities fall to individuals, communities, and institutions?

references.label: 1 · Luke 10:30–37 · Mercy made practical
references.note: Read the Samaritan’s response to an injured stranger: attention to wounds, transport, shelter, payment, and continued responsibility. Compare this with the compilation’s calls for tenderness, competent treatment, and service to the poor. What does the story reveal about the work involved in becoming a neighbor to someone who suffers?

subjects.displayTitle: The Word and human limits: understanding, humility, and response
subjects.introduction: A single word can open a world of meaning without placing that world in our hands. Bahá’u’lláh pictures the Word of God as a cup whose wine lies hidden, as an ocean folded within one letter, as a river of names that must be crossed before the sea of meaning is reached. The humbling lesson is that the profoundest thinker and the holiest saint never step outside the circle of their own conceptions, and that a finite mind cannot encompass the Creator of whom it is itself a sign. Yet this is no counsel of despair. Knowing what cannot be grasped becomes a discipline of attention: the joyful recitation of one verse, fair judgment of unfamiliar claims, a heart made pure enough to hear. Paul’s picture of knowing in part and seeing through a glass [1] asks how such awareness might soften both the way we study and the way we treat one another. The path leads on into the limits of language and of the intellect, the unknowability of God, and the puzzle of a Word at once near and abstruse, until understanding is measured by a good word and a righteous deed.
subjects.arc: Open with meaning beyond names and the fruit of understanding; examine finite knowledge, receptive reading and claims of revelation; end with humility, inquiry and action.

order.why: Examine the limits of even profound human conceptions.
shortened: To whatever heights the mind of the most exalted of men may soar, however great the depths which the detached and understanding heart can penetrate, such mind and heart can never transcend that which is the creature of their own conceptions and the product of their own thoughts.
Whoever pondereth this truth in his heart will readily admit that there are certain limits which no human being can possibly transgress.

order.why: Open with the movement from names toward meanings.
Offer the cup and its contents as an image for reading.
Ask immediately how understanding bears fruit in words and deeds.
shortened: One goodly word and one righteous deed are, in this Day, more precious in the sight of God than all the books of the earth - namely, those books which the heedless divines have written according to their vain imaginings.

order.why: Value the quality of recitation above its quantity.
Introduce acknowledgment of limitation as an achievement of insight.
Distinguish knowledge of signs from encompassing their Creator.
shortened: The all-encompassing must assuredly be greater than that which is encompassed, and thus the latter can in no wise discover the former or comprehend its reality. No matter how far human minds may advance, even attaining the highest degree of human comprehension, the uttermost limit of this comprehension is to behold the signs and attributes of God in the world of creation and not in the realm of Divinity.

order.why: Keep fair reading and justice in view.
shortened: He hath come unto you from the heaven of bounty with the Kingdom of verses and the Dominion of clear proofs, with a sovereignty that encompasseth all worlds. Read ye what hath been sent down from His presence - verily it guideth you unto a path that is straight through justice.

order.why: Imagine depth within a single letter.
shortened: Thus have We sent down the verses and dispatched them unto thee. By the life of God! Within each letter thereof lieth concealed an ocean of meanings and utterance, were men to know.

order.why: Introduce speech measured to what listeners can bear.
shortened: He speaks the truth in the Kingdom of Utterance according to a measured degree, and remains silent concerning that which the ears of men cannot bear to hear. Verily, He is the All-Wise One Who speaks with measure.

order.why: Relate the extent of disclosure to capacity.
Explore repeated words, differing meanings and accommodation to listeners.
shortened: And whenever We have repeated words, We have intended in each one of them a meaning that none hath comprehended save My all-knowing and informed Self. By thy life! Had We found the people to have attained maturity, We would not have repeated the words.
But since We have found their souls accustomed to fancy and imitation, therefore doth the Pen of Command reveal that which befitteth the condition of these weak ones.

order.why: Retain the Gospel allusion and its supplied citation exactly.
shortened: For they are as children, so far as knowledge is concerned. They are unable to bear the higher realities revealed from the Merciful Kingdom: as Christ (upon Him is Glory!) said in the text of the Gospel. "I have yet many things to tell you but ye cannot bear them now" (John 16:18).

order.why: Read restraint in disclosure amid danger and hope.
Notice the offer of another explanation in another language.
Keep the reported historical claim about translation distinctly attributed.
Consider examples and the invitation to read dispensations toward their fulfillment.
Introduce the disproportion between intended meaning and comprehension.
Extend the limit from created things to the divine Essence.
shortened: So perfect and  comprehensive is His creation that no mind nor heart, however keen or pure, can ever grasp the nature of the most insignificant of His creatures; much less fathom the mystery of Him Who is the Day Star of Truth, Who is the invisible and unknowable Essence.

The conceptions of the devoutest of mystics, the attainments of the most accomplished amongst men, the highest praise which human tongue or pen can render are all the product of man’s finite mind and are conditioned by its limitations.

order.why: Examine the relation between a concept and the mind that contains it.
shortened: Now concerning the Essence of Divinity: in truth it is on no account determined by anything apart from its own nature, and can in no wise be comprehended. For whatsoever can be conceived by man is a reality that hath limitations and is not unlimited; it is circumscribed, not all-embracing. It can be comprehended by man, and is controlled by him.

order.why: Read the same issue through imagination and capacity.
shortened: Things which are understood by men cannot be outside their capacity for understanding, so that it is impossible for the heart of man to comprehend the nature of the Majesty of God. Our imagination can only picture that which it is able to create.

order.why: Follow the argument contrasting finite and unlimited reality.
shortened: Therefore, the reality of Divinity in its identity is beyond the range of human intellection because the human mind, the human intellect, the human thought are limited, whereas the reality of Divinity is unlimited. How can the limited grasp the unlimited and transcend it? Impossible. The unlimited always comprehends the limited. The limited can never comprehend, surround nor take in the unlimited. Therefore, every concept of Divinity which has come within the intellection of a human being is finite, or limited, and is a pure product of imagination, whereas the reality of Divinity is holy and sacred above and beyond all such concepts.

order.why: Condense that contrast into drop and ocean.
shortened: No matter how far the human intelligence may advance, it is still but a drop, while divine omniscience is the ocean.

order.why: Read the reported contrast between human need and divine power.
shortened: Man is limited, weak, fearful, poverty-stricken and helpless. The Divine Reality represents the Power Absolute, capacity for all things, fulfillment for all the needs of man.

order.why: Include the unfathomability of grace and mercy.
shortened: No man can ever claim to have comprehended the nature of the hidden and manifold grace of God; none can fathom His all-embracing mercy.

order.why: Allow invisible realms to enlarge the horizon of inquiry.
shortened: Know then that the Lord God possesseth invisible realms which the human intellect can never hope to fathom nor the mind of man conceive.

order.why: Consider the warning against denying whatever ordinary reason cannot grasp.
shortened: 68 God, the Most High, hath placed these signs in men so that veiled minds might not deny the mysteries of the life beyond, nor belittle that which hath been promised them. For some hold fast to reason and deny whatever reason comprehendeth not, and yet feeble minds can never grasp the reality of the stages that we have related: The universal divine Intellect alone can comprehend them.

order.why: Examine the argument that finite reason is not an infallible criterion.
shortened: This is a clear proof that human reason is not to be relied upon as an infallible criterion.

If we are not endowed with perfect reason, how can we comprehend the meanings of the Word of God? Therefore, human reason, as already pointed out, is by its very nature finite and faulty in conclusions. It cannot surround the Reality Itself, the Infinite Word.

order.why: Preserve the text’s historical examples within its argument about disagreement.
shortened: The second criterion is that of the intellect, which was the principal criterion of comprehension for those pillars of wisdom, the ancient philosophers. They deduced things through the power of the mind and relied on rational arguments: all their arguments are based upon reason. But despite this, they diverged greatly in their opinions.

Even Plato at first proved through rational arguments the immobility of the earth and the movement of the sun, and then subsequently established, again through rational arguments, the centrality of the sun and the movement of the earth.

order.why: Distinguish external argument from the experience described as inward vision.
shortened: These are theoretical arguments adduced for weak souls, but if the eye of inner vision be opened, a hundred thousand clear proofs will be seen. Thus, when man feels the indwelling spirit, he is in no need of arguments for its existence; but for those who are deprived of the grace of the spirit, it is necessary to set forth external arguments.

order.why: Read the claim that intellectual development alone does not complete human education.
shortened: By mere intellectual development and power of reason, man cannot attain to his fullest degree—that is to say, by means of intellect alone he cannot accomplish the progress effected by religion. For the philosophers of the past strove in vain to revivify the world of mankind through the intellectual faculty. The most of which they were capable was educating themselves and a limited number of disciples; they themselves have confessed failure. Therefore, the world of humanity must be confirmed by the breath of the Holy Spirit in order to receive universal education.

order.why: Explore the lamp’s need for light in that account of education.
shortened: The chimney of the lamp, no matter how polished and perfect it be, is in need of the light. Without the light, the lamp or candle is not illuminating. Without the spirit, the body is not productive. The teacher of material principles is limited. The philosophers who claimed to be the educators of mankind were at most only able to train themselves. If they educated others, it was within a restricted circle; they failed to bestow general education and development. This has been conferred upon humanity by the power of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Keep the recorded claim about the limits of philosophical influence attributed.
shortened: What I mean is this -- philosophy and science will not suffice to elevate and civilize a people who are in a bestial condition.
Philosophy of necessity is restricted to a small school and cannot have an essentially moral influence.

order.why: Consider the reported difficulty of knowing all requirements of human life.
Explains the limits of human comprehension of the Word.
Retain the reported account of unity and limitation.
Read the suggestion that the human reality exceeds attempted description.
Notice differing experiences among seekers of truth.
shortened: O divine lover! The seekers of truth and the yearners for the Absolute Beauty sought the rising of the Sun of Truth in the horizons of the world and within themselves. Some beheld a gleam, others a flame, while some became bewildered and wandered astray.

order.why: Enter the extended inquiry into learning, recognition and the veil of knowledge.
shortened: We have consumed this densest of all veils with the fire of the love of the Beloved -- the veil referred to in the saying: "The most grievous of all veils is the veil of knowledge."

The understanding of His words and the comprehension of the utterances of the Birds of Heaven are in no wise dependent upon human learning. They depend solely upon purity of heart, chastity of soul, and freedom of spirit.

order.why: Question the easy identification of social learning with spiritual understanding.
Keep the recorded Nicodemus example as a particular interpretation.
Attend to the obstacle of blind imitation.
shortened: Say: Whosoever doth not cleanse his heart of the veils of blind imitation shall be unable to approach this sublime, irradiant Face.

order.why: Examine hearing shaped by inherited stories and assumptions.
Consider the persistence of newly adopted veils.
Ask what happens when a name becomes an object of devotion.
shortened: Every sect among the sects hath taken unto itself one of the names and made it lord for itself besides God. Thus have their souls beguiled them.

order.why: Develop the image of drowning in names beside a present ocean.
Contrast verbal mention with inward images.
shortened: They that have turned away - these shall have no portion. They make mention of God with their tongues while their hearts tell of images and idols.

order.why: Read the burning of fancies through love.
shortened: Today the Dawning-Place of Revelation and the Source of Divine inspiration hath appeared and shone forth from the horizon of the heaven of God's loving-kindness. Yet the people of the earth remain heedless and veiled from it, save those souls who have burned away the veils of fancy and idle imaginings with the fire of the love of God, exalted be His glory, and have become free and detached from all else but Him.

order.why: Join freedom from imaginings with an active turning of the heart.
shortened: Every soul that rises up for the sake of God in that very moment enters the presence of the Intended One and finds the Beloved through the fragrance of hearts.
God willing, through the grace of the All-Merciful, may you be free at all times from idle fancies and imaginings, and be attentive and turned toward the direction of certitude.

order.why: Consider learned authority as a possible veil.
shortened: Blessed is the soul whom neither the veils of the divines nor the clouds of the jurisprudents have withheld from the Most Exalted Horizon.

order.why: Read the contrast between illuminating wisdom and following an unknowing guide.
Ask how imagining can obstruct response to a gift.
shortened: Did ye but know what He desireth for you, ye would hasten unto Him with your very eyes. But ye are held back through following vain imaginings.

order.why: Keep the terse reversal of apparent benefit and harm.
Turn attention from blaming the light to examining vision.
shortened: Is this Light a veil? Nay, by My Self, rather it is your own eyes that are veiled, O people of the Book!

order.why: Notice passing and hearing without recognition.
Develop the paradox of a speaking Book that goes unheard.
shortened: By God! The Book speaketh, yet the people hear not. The rock hath cried out, and the cry hath been raised, and all things have spoken, yet the people understand not.

order.why: Hear the similar contrast between glad tidings and inattention.
Retain the Sinai image in the account of failed hearing.
Widen speech to the atoms of creation.
shortened: This is a Day wherein all atoms speak even as the Tongue of Grandeur and Glory hath spoken, yet most of the people remain heedless.

order.why: Set moved mountains beside human unawareness.
Attend to the many images of utterance and missed perception.
Hear the Tablet’s lament alongside the speaking Book.
shortened: Verily the Book speaketh, yet the people hear not; and the Pen warbleth, yet mankind knoweth not; and the Tablet lamenteth over what hath befallen the Cause of God, the Lord of all being, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Consider the text’s accumulation of signs and continuing heedlessness.
Read the image of sleep despite revealed evidence.
shortened: He hath sent down the verses and revealed the evidences, yet the people remain in a strange sleep.

order.why: Consider the rarity of receptive ears amid abundant utterance.
shortened: Night and day its shrill voice is raised, yet ears capable of hearing are rarer than the red elixir. The revelation has encompassed all possibility and divine verses have descended like torrential rain, yet ignorant servants cling to vain imaginings and hold fast to calumnies.

order.why: Turn criticism toward a plea that people not be deprived.
shortened: Most wondrous of all is the heedlessness of the servants and the tyranny of them that dwell in the lands. We beseech God not to deprive His servants of the outpourings of the Day of Retribution, nor to withhold from them the hearing of His Word and the beholding of His Horizon.

order.why: Invite contemplation of differing conditions of faith.
Associate understanding with sincerity.
shortened: They whose eyes are illumined with the light of understanding will perceive the sweet savors of the All-Merciful, and will embrace His truth. These are they who are truly sincere.

order.why: Consider listening as inward spiritual quickening.
shortened: And thou, O handmaiden of God, hearken unto the holy, divine melodies, that through hearing them the Holy Spirit may be raised up in thy heart and the Spirit of Power may speak in thy breast.

order.why: Make pondering an active part of drawing near.
shortened: By God! Whoso pondereth today, the melodies of the All-Merciful will draw him to the heaven of good-pleasure and purify him from human limitations and bring him nigh unto the Most Great Prospect.

order.why: Read silence as a preparation for hearing.
Preserve the invitation to refined hearing and tasting.
shortened: The former shall forever speak and the latter shall forever flow.
May thy honor hearken unto it with a pure ear and taste thereof at all times with a refined palate.

order.why: Imagine longing changing the listener’s direction.
shortened: Among the people is he who, upon hearing the verses of God, is so seized by the rapture of longing that he forsaketh all who dwell on earth and turneth with his heart unto God, the Mighty, the Wise.

order.why: Read the snow-and-sun image of longing.
shortened: By God! Wert thou to become aware of its greatness and the greatness of the station of Him Who manifesteth it, thou wouldst melt away with the fire of longing even as snow melteth from the heat of the sun.

order.why: Explore utterance as strength for perseverance.
shortened: This is a Book sent down in truth on this Day unto him who hath believed in God, the Supreme Ruler, the Self-Subsisting, that the rapture of its utterance may so seize him that no one shall be able to deter him from the path of God, the Lord of all existence. We have indeed expounded the mysteries of the Book and revealed that which lay hidden in the knowledge of God, whereunto bear witness His favored servants.

order.why: Attend to attraction and certitude as aims of revelation.
shortened: In all days doth move the Pen of the Lord of all names that hearts may be attracted by its traces, and in every night doth speak the tongue of Revelation that perchance men may attain certitude through God's verses.

order.why: Recognize remembrance and response within the verses.
Receive a personal address from imprisonment with gratitude.
Read the value assigned to a revealed address.
shortened: All the treasures of the world cannot compare with what hath been revealed concerning you. This is from God's grace which He bestoweth upon whomsoever He willeth.

order.why: Keep the speaker’s sense of inadequacy before a letter.
shortened: O my Beloved! This letter, whose very point merits such description and is worthy of such praise - how can this perishable frame prove equal to answering it or venture to make response?

order.why: Notice a comparison with rain followed by an acknowledgment of its inadequacy.
shortened: In secret, with utmost supplication I was saying: Would that all the world were present to attain unto the hearing of the revealed verses which flow and descend like pouring rain. I seek God's forgiveness for this comparison, I seek His forgiveness and turn unto Him.

order.why: Retain the reported contrast between earthly music and divine melody.
Encounter repeated lamps and crystals as a language of radiance.
Read the relations of suns, moons and stars in the imagery of wisdom.
Consider shelter as another way of describing the Word.
Read the name adorning the heaven of utterance.
Enter the praise of utterance as creative command.
Read the reply that places the origin of nature in the divine Word.
shortened: Hearken unto what the idolaters say, that these verses were not revealed naturally. Say: Open your eyes, O company of the heedless ones! By God, by a single letter of what hath been sent down from the dominion of God, the Mighty, the Bountiful, nature and its sources and its manifestations were created.

order.why: Explore letters imagined as voices between earth and heaven.
Retain the startling images of resurrection and distinction.
Hear the affirmation of the Word’s penetrating power.
Consider the comparison with the influence of human speech.
shortened: Glory be to God! In the Tablet of Wisdom mention is made of the penetrating power of the Word. God, our Lord and the Lord of the mighty Throne and the elevated Seat, speaketh the truth. This servant beareth witness that the word of the loved ones courseth and floweth through and penetrateth all elements - how much more so the Most Exalted Word of God! This evanescent one is incapable of describing its effect and penetrating power.

order.why: Read attraction and nearness as effects of utterance.
shortened: Say: Through His utterance all things were attracted, through His call the names were set ablaze, and through His remembrance the near ones drew nigh unto a station which was raised up through the name of Truth.

order.why: Acknowledge the stated abundance beyond reckoning.
shortened: The verses have been sent down in such wise that the sincere ones are powerless to reckon them.

order.why: Consider the claim of continually renewed utterance.
shortened: Today the divine verses have encompassed all things, and from the Dayspring of divine revelation at every moment there appears and rises a utterance the like of which the eye of the world and the ears of nations have never seen or heard.

order.why: Distinguish enduring divine speech from passing circumstances.
shortened: This is among His great favors, for verily every word that hath issued from the mouth of the Divine Will and been recorded by the Most Exalted Pen shall endure and remain forever.

order.why: Read the contrast between the Word and monuments.
Hear the continuing summons toward God.
shortened: Verily the Pen of the Most Merciful moves at all times and calls out with the most exalted call to all who dwell in the realm of creation, summoning all to God in their return.

order.why: Identify proclamation as the Pen’s purpose.
shortened: O Most Exalted Pen! The Lord of Names declares: Thou wert created for the purpose of proclamation. This is the Day whereon thou must give glad tidings of the appearance of the Lord of all creation to all the friends and guide them to the straight path of God.

order.why: Consider the universal reach of the Book’s invitation.
shortened: This is a Book which the All-Merciful hath sent down for all who are in the realm of possibility, that it may draw all to God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Read hearing as a movement toward the horizon.
shortened: O people of the earth! Hearken unto the call of the Lord of Heaven, for verily it will draw you nigh unto the supreme horizon, that station wherein the Divine Lote Tree proclaimeth: The kingdom belongeth unto God, the Single, the One, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Retain the invitation to heed the decisive Word.
Gather hearing, sight, drinking and attainment together.
shortened: The Book is revealed, the Fountain is flowing, the Hidden is manifest, and the Promised One speaks. Turn ye with clear certitude that ye may hear and see and drink and attain.

order.why: Read the announcement of the Hidden made manifest.
shortened: Take it with the hand of power and say: By God! That which was hidden behind the veils of the Unseen hath appeared, and the Nightingale of Immortality hath warbled upon the branches. The Hidden One hath been made manifest and God hath come with a mighty Cause.

order.why: Hear the Book itself announce fulfillment.
shortened: Verily the Book crieth out before the faces of the world: The Hidden One hath appeared, Who was concealed from eyes and inscribed in the Books of God, the Lord of Lords.

order.why: Consider the new ornament given to the world.
Read the urgency of a new dawn’s summons.
Place knowledge within the language of grace and generosity.
Hear the acknowledgment of sovereignty in the Book of utterance.
shortened: This is the Book of utterance which the All-Merciful has sent down from the Kingdom of mystic knowledge to those who have believed in Him in His days and have testified to that which His Most Exalted Pen has testified: The Kingdom, the Dominion, the Grandeur and the Might belong unto God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Introduce the Word presented in human temple.
Preserve the source’s call and announced manifestation.
shortened: Verily We hear at this hour the Call which hath been raised betwixt earth and heaven, as though the Caller were God, the Lord of all worlds. And when We turned toward it with Our most pure hearing, We heard it say: "O concourse of humanity! By God, the Most Great Spectacle hath appeared, and God hath made it the seat of His mighty Throne.

order.why: Read fulfillment alongside the disclosure of inward motives.
Retain the mustard-seed allusion as an image of what becomes manifest.
shortened: In these days the mystery of what the All-Merciful revealed in the Qur'an is made manifest, His blessed and exalted Word: "Though it be but the weight of a mustard seed and though it be hidden in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, God will bring it to light."

order.why: Keep the diverse responses to resurrection imagery visible.
shortened: When the trumpet was blown and the tombs arose, the people were shaken: among them were those who were bewildered, those who swooned away, and those who took wing in their longing for the appearance of God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Keep the reported explanation of compressed time attributed.
shortened: When He says "The Day of Resurrection is fifty thousand years," it means matters that would take fifty thousand years to occur or be achieved will be manifested in one day in the Day of Manifestation.

order.why: Explore many Books through the recurring image of one sun.
shortened: I testify that the likeness of the Books of God is as the likeness of the sun - though it rise countless times, it is but one sun, and though it set countless times, it is but one sun. Similarly, though Books be revealed from God times without number, they are but one Book, and though they be raised up times without number, they are raised up unto God and are but one Book. I testify that the Book is the Word of God from the Sun of Truth in every Dispensation, howsoever God willeth and in whatsoever tongue He revealeth it.

order.why: Read the historical theological argument about recognizing a succeeding revelation.
shortened: All have been created for the meeting with the Face of God; and it is nigh that, in the very reality of truth, the mediation of the Names shall be attained. Yet the mirrors have not recognized their own reflection, and they imagine unity through the effulgent Revelation that preceded Him, which appeared in the Muhammadan Temple -- peace be upon Him -- whereas that Revelation hath been lifted up, even as, at the advent of the Messenger of God, the dispensation of Moses, the Spirit of God, was lifted up.

order.why: Turn the danger of being veiled by the former revelation into prayer.
shortened: For all who are veiled are veiled by what Thou didst ordain before. Therefore have mercy, O my God, upon those who profess Thy unity, that they may follow Thy Manifestation on the Day of Resurrection and not be veiled by the manifestation before it, for all are from Thee and Thou art the All-Knowing, the Wondrous.

order.why: Consider earlier expectations reinterpreted by a new manifestation.
shortened: Consider also the words of the Letters and the Gates concerning the appearance of the Qa'im. Yet at the time of His wondrous manifestation all these sayings were set aside by a single word, as thou thyself bearest witness that the Prophet hath been from the beginning that hath no beginning and will continue unto the end that hath no end, as mentioned in the words of the Exalted One - may the life of all else be a sacrifice unto Him.

order.why: Retain the reply to a claim about repeated verses.
shortened: When the verses were sent down, they said: "These were revealed before in the tongue of the Remembrance." Nay, they are among the fabricators.

order.why: Preserve the reported objections about apparent inconsistency.
Keep the polemic about professed loyalty and actual treatment in its setting.
Read the appeal to the present day against a return to former expectations.
Consider the disparity between a promise and its reception.
Ask how claimed steadfastness can be disturbed.
Attend to the warning about events and doubts becoming veils.
shortened: Beware lest the happenings of the world prevent thee from the Ancient Beauty or the doubts of the nations veil thee from this irrevocable Cause.

order.why: Follow with the call to set worldly conditions behind.
shortened: Beware lest the conditions of the world withhold you from the Most Great Name. Cast them behind you, turning unto God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Read recognition as release from blame.
shortened: Had men recognized the excellence of this Day, they would have cast blame behind their backs, turning unto God, the Lord of all mankind.

order.why: Examine the Book of Names’ appeal to reading, proof and guidance.
shortened: Ye dwell in your homes, holding a Book in your hands, reading what is therein, yet ye perceive not that this is from God Who created you, sustaineth you, causeth you to die, and giveth you life. It hath been sent down by Him Whom God shall make manifest unto you, that ye might be guided by His appearance. Why do ye not understand a matter when ye read it, failing to be guided by the proofs contained therein?

order.why: Read the stated sufficiency of a single verse.
shortened: Say: God is the Hidden of all hidden, if ye be of them that magnify His remembrance. Doth not that Book suffice you wherein is the decree of all things? Will ye not then be thankful? Say: A single verse sufficeth as a proof from God unto all who are in the heavens and on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, would ye but know it.

order.why: Preserve the claim of the verses’ inimitability.
Keep the separate prayerful affirmation of that claim.
Consider the significance assigned to one revealed letter.
Set the claim of each word’s greatness beside the question of receptivity.
shortened: In this Revelation, every word that hath dawned from the horizon of the Will of God, glory be to His majesty, all mention, nay all books, bow down before it. Where is the vision to see, and where is the hearing to hear, and where is the heart to understand?

order.why: Read the appeal for a consistent standard in judging revelation.
shortened: He hath come with the hosts of divine revelation and inspiration, and hath manifested that which lay hidden in the treasuries of His knowledge and stored in the repositories of His might. Thereupon the servants and dwellers of the lands rose up in rejection and protest, to such extent that they denied the Books of God and His Scriptures and whatsoever was revealed aforetime unto His Prophets and Messengers. Say: O people of the earth! Be fair in the name of God - if ye deny this Most Great Cause and this Mighty Announcement, by what proof can ye establish that which ye possess?

order.why: Make fairness explicit at the point of judgment.
shortened: Say: O people! Fear ye God, then judge with fairness concerning that which hath appeared in truth from One Who is powerful and ancient. He speaketh not of His own desire, but rather from God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Retain the text’s account of individual proof in its polemical context.
Preserve the severe scriptural comparison without adopting it as an editorial judgment.
Keep the historical dispute over testing and proof tied to its speaker.
shortened: Know that Javad Qazvini wrote in his Persian letter according to what he wrote from the realms of hell with false words, including that testing the proof from the followers of God's family, peace be upon them, necessitates the testing of the Prophet - may the peace and blessings of God be upon Him and His family - and verily the testing of the Prophet necessitates the testing of the Lord, exalted be His glory. This is manifest unbelief, yet most people do not understand.

order.why: Read the rebuke to a particular question in its original address.
shortened: Know then that there hath come before the Divine Throne thy letter wherein thou didst make mention of thyself, and toward which were directed the glances of thy Lord, the Lord of all worlds. Therein didst thou ask that which befitteth neither thy station nor the station of any in the heavens and earth. Dost thou question Him by Whose command all that was and shall be hath appeared? Him Who created all things by His word "Be," and it was, if thou be of them that understand?

order.why: Hold the invitation to search the Tablets beside the statement about the time for questions.
Distinguish knowledge of commandments from the recognition sought by the text.
shortened: If you say the decisive verses are the divine commandments revealed in the Tablets, there is no doubt in this - we all are assured of them, believe in them, and hope for His grace. These decisive verses are decisive in relation to the Most Wise of Judges, as it is evident that if a person were to comprehend all the decisive verses but hesitate even slightly in accepting that Most Great Verse, all his deeds would yield no fruit and would be as dust.

order.why: Read the challenge to reliance on sciences, possessions and glory.
shortened: Your sciences shall not profit you in this day, nor your arts, nor your treasures, nor your glory. Cast them  all behind your backs, and set your faces towards the Most Sublime Word through which the Scriptures and the Books and this lucid Tablet have been distinctly set forth.

order.why: Keep the parallel warning about books and treasures.
Consider acceptance as a response demanded by the passage.
shortened: Cast away what ye possess and turn unto the Singular, the All-Informed. On this Day, no soul's belief shall profit it except after its acceptance.

order.why: Read the direction to attend to the Pen’s utterance.
Place commandments within the imagery of loving-kindness.
shortened: Verily My commandments are the lamps of My loving-kindness amidst My creation and the sweet-scented savors of My raiment in My kingdom. Blessed is he who attaineth unto them, and woe betide those who turn away.

order.why: Retain the source’s injunction concerning speech.
shortened: No one is permitted to utter a word except as ordained by God in the Most Holy Book which hath been sent down from the kingdom of My wondrous utterance.

order.why: Connect recognition with keeping a covenant.
shortened: Beware, O people of the earth, lest ye abandon that which ye have been commanded to observe, or break the covenant ye have made in My holy and impregnable presence.

order.why: Explore worship beyond recompense and beyond a conception of the Essence.
shortened: Whosoever worships His Essence without attention to aught else in His creation, and without desire for any recompense save Him, has truly worshipped God in the manner possible within the realm of contingency. One must be certain that the Essence in its essence was and is beyond description, recognition, or worship.

Should anyone worship Him or call upon Him in hope of paradise or fear of hell-fire, he has indeed been veiled from true worship of God and is unworthy of His Essence. Rather, the way of worship is to worship Him according to how He has described Himself, without mention of aught else.

order.why: Retain the description of motion beyond ordinary spatial opposition.
shortened: Although this motion is mentioned as opposed to rest, yet it is sanctified from ascent and descent, and is exalted above vacillation and the comprehension of them that are bounded by limitations.

order.why: Include the distinction between decreed and conditional events.
shortened: I say in truth that there hath never been and shall never be any barrier against the decreed hour. Thus He saith that death shall overtake every soul, even if they be in lofty, impregnable towers. But that which is not decreed may be lifted through God's absolute Will and His pervading divine Purpose.

order.why: Read accountability against the passing of worldly life.
Recognize suffering endured for a religious purpose.
Preserve the mundane household request, allowing the full source selection to retain its particularity.
shortened: One night among those nights, Khwajeh Ilyas 'Abbud, in whose house the Throne is now established, attained the Most Holy Presence, and after seeing the dishes, at one point asked this servant whether it would be possible to write and have brought one set of coffee cups with one covered soup bowl from the Chinese dishes.

order.why: Offer reassurance amid passing affairs.
shortened: Let not the affairs of the world grieve thee. By My life! They shall pass away, and thou shalt witness what hath been ordained for those near unto God.

order.why: Distinguish turning the heart from a physically prohibited journey.
shortened: Say: The path of God hath appeared - hasten ye unto it and be not of them that tarry.

We have ordained that hearts should turn towards Him - know ye this and be not of those who turn their feet toward this praiseworthy Station. Indeed He hath not permitted them to do so, lest there arise a clamor among the people.

order.why: Bring the inquiry toward services undertaken for everyone’s benefit.
Return knowledge to a personal acknowledgment and blessing.
Pray in awareness of what minds cannot attain.
shortened: Glorified, glorified art Thou from the hearts of Thy servants reaching unto Thee or the minds of Thy creatures attaining the seat of Thy glory!

order.why: End the source-linked sequence with acknowledgment of limited knowledge of one’s own good.
shortened: I know not what lieth with Thee or what shall benefit me, but with Thee is the knowledge of all things in a perspicuous Book.

order.why: Open the supplied readings with encouragement to study alongside limits on imagining the next world.
shortened: Regarding your question concerning a deep and profound study of the teachings: of course the Baha'is can and should meditate upon the significances of the writings, and endeavour to grasp their meaning to the utmost.... However certain things are, by their very nature, a mystery to us, at least in our present stage of development. One of these is what the next world, the purely spiritual world, is like.         To try and visualize that realm in the terms of this physical one is absolutely impossible.

order.why: Locate partial understanding within an early stage of religious history.
Consider how human interpretation permits error and disagreement.
Retain the brief supplied excerpt on the limits of scientific statements.
Place those limits beside the explicit principle of harmony between religion and science.
Preserve the provisional passage honoring intellect while examining its dependence on experience.
Read the supplied warning about learning as a veil.
Explore the provisional distinction between intellect and heart.
Apply that distinction to the problem of freedom and destiny.
shortened: Indeed, all who have endeavoured to explain the problem of Destiny have advocated either absolute divine determinism or human choice, and thus all the philosophers have confessed their powerlessness to explain the truth of this question. Indeed, this verily is the truth, inasmuch as the philosophers wanted to explain the divine truth, the Middle Path between absolute determinism and absolute freedom, by proofs of reason, which is, however, impossible. For, verily, reason, even in its utmost level of abstraction, is confined to understanding mere limited phenomenona, which fail to guide humans unto the summit of the delight of their heart.

order.why: Keep the supplied Plotinus excerpt’s question about describing simplicity.
Retain the supplied commentary’s distinction between divine absence and presence.
Close with the question of response when the rationale of a command remains unclear.

questions: How do the images of cup and wine, names and meanings, or drop and ocean change the way you approach a text?
What is the difference between acknowledging the limits of understanding and abandoning the effort to understand?
How might education, inherited expectations, or attachment to a vocabulary both assist and obstruct recognition?
What habits of listening and judgment do these passages ask of a reader confronting unfamiliar claims?
How can confidence in a sacred text coexist with humility about one’s interpretation and openness to another reader?
What would a good word, a righteous deed, or service for everyone’s benefit reveal about the understanding one has gained?

references.note: Read Paul’s images of childhood, partial knowledge, and seeing through a glass, together with his emphasis on faith, hope, and love. Compare them with the compilation’s distinction between human comprehension and divine reality. How might the awareness of partial knowledge shape both the way we study and the way we treat one another?
